picks.headline: Ducks Wire staff predicts Oregon Ducks vs. Northwestern Wildcats
picks.blurb: That seems like a long time ago, doesn't it? Less than a week later, we are sitting with the Ducks at 4-3, having just fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following another loss, and quarterback Dante Moore announcing that his 2026 season is over after the concussion he suffered earlier this year against USC. Now, with a laundry list of questions to answer, the Ducks go forward into a brutal home matchup against the No. 20 Northwestern Wildcats , hoping that they can somehow manage to get back to their winning ways. To preview the game, we go through our weekly roundtable with the writers from Ducks Wire to offer our opinions and predictions for what's to come. Here is our roundtable conversation. Question: Well, it's certainly been an eventful week in Eugene. Let's start with the biggest news: Dante Moore is not expected to play again this season. With the Ducks sitting at 4-3 and their playoff hopes essentially gone, what are your expectations for the rest of the season? What would a successful finish look like? Zachary Neel: At this point, a successful season is going 7-5 on the year and making it to a semi-respectable bowl game when all is said and done, and that's incredibly sad to say, considering where this season started. Just about everything has gone wrong for Oregon thus far, and I truly do see a reality where they struggle to even become bowl-eligible. But I think the culture wins out, and Dan Lanning can rally this team over the final five weeks. Bjorn Bergstrom: The culture that we’ve come to know in recent seasons is of a team that stays together and fights, no matter the circumstances. That hasn’t been the case in 2026, but if they can reclaim that fight and grittiness, then I think that should be considered a success. The way things are going, it’s hard to stamp “success” on a certain win total. It’s more about the process and the eye test, rather than the end result. Logan Brown: It’s hard to find any success in this season at this point. I guess if Oregon beats Washington, that’s probably the least you could ask for? I would say an 8-4 finish would mean the Ducks played well in November and finished strong, but that probably means losses to Northwestern and Ohio State. It’s probably going to get worse before it gets any better. Drew Mehringer Question: Dan Lanning made one of the biggest decisions of his coaching career on Sunday, firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer after Oregon's loss to Illinois. Do you agree with the decision, and how much of the blame for Oregon's offensive struggles falls on Mehringer compared to the players and other coaches? Zachary Neel: I think a change needed to be made, but I also don't think this change is going to lead to a switch being flipped for the Oregon offense. The problems go much deeper than just the play calling, in my opinion, and I don't think we're going to all of a sudden see the Ducks putting up 27-31 points per game because Mehringer is no longer in the building. As the OC, he was rightfully the guy to fall on the sword, but more changes are needed this offseason. Bjorn Bergstrom: It's hard not to agree with the decision. Fans had been on him from the very beginning, it seemed, but I was finally on board after last week’s debacle. As far as the blame, there’s some that goes to the position coaches who didn’t have their guys ready to play individually, but the play calls were what stuck out to me in particular. It didn’t seem like Mehringer had the ability to scheme up easy looks for his quarterbacks and easy running holes for his backs. There was a clear lack of creativity. Just watch any other top-25 team in college football and you’ll see the difference in outside-of-the-box thinking schematically that Mehringer just couldn’t manage to implement. Logan Brown: Unfortunately, I do feel like it was the right move. There were so many times where it just seemed like the offense was lacking situational awareness because of the play call. I lost count of the amount of times the Ducks ran a third down play, from any distance, where receivers were all running routes short of the sticks. There were zero aggressive calls, and more aiming and carefully crafting open receivers to the point where if the defense had an answer, there was no counter. I do think Oregon’s lack of offensive line and quarterback development has played a significant role in the offense’s struggles, but Mehringer was a clear issue that the Ducks could do something about midseason. New Play-Caller Question: Jay Johnson is taking over play-calling duties for the Ducks, and he'll have quite the challenge trying to turn this offense around. What's the biggest change you hope to see from Oregon's offense under Johnson? And realistically, how much improvement can we expect in just one week? Zachary Neel: Asking Johnson to come in and completely change this offense is unfair and unrealistic. I think at the best, you can hope that Oregon's offensive scheme looks more simplified, leaning more heavily on running between the tackles, finding a rhythm, and getting the ball past the sticks on down-and-distance situations. But as far as an entirely new scheme that looks different from what we've seen over the past seven weeks, I'm not expecting that. Bjorn Bergstrom: The biggest thing I’ll be wanting to see is more creativity in the passing game as far as Dylan Raiola’s platform, whether it be rolling him out, sprint-outs, or moving the pocket so it’s not a straight dropback. Moving the quarterback in the backfield makes it so much more difficult for a defense to pinpoint where he’ll be on a given play, opening up the run game at the same time as they’ll be just a step slower. Also, no more Wildcat. Yuck. Logan Brown: Take some chances! Oregon has nothing to lose at this point. The Ducks have Ferraris all over the offense, but most throws are horizontal or short of the sticks. Safeties play close to the line because the Ducks don’t trust their quarterback to air it out. At this point, the season is gone, so why not air it out? Why not run more counters and try to produce explosive plays on the ground? I don't think Johnson changes a ton in just one week, but I do think he could set the tone with a different plan on critical downs. Question: Northwestern comes to Eugene at 6-1, ranked No. 20 in the nation, with former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly running the offense. The Wildcats have been one of the biggest surprises in the Big Ten this season. What concerns you most about this matchup, and where do you think Northwestern has the biggest advantage over Oregon? Zachary Neel: Any time Oregon faces a true dual-threat quarterback who can beat you with his feet, Duck fans get worried. That has been the Achilles heel in Eugene for years, and Aidan Chiles is as good at that as anyone. With his ability both in the air and on the ground, plus Chip Kelly's offensive mind, I know that the Ducks' defense is going to have its hands full on Saturday. Bjorn Bergstrom: I think that Northwestern has a simple, yet very important advantage: they play sound, complementary football much, much better than the Ducks have this season. They’ve been a complete team, complimenting each other on offense, defense and special teams and picking up for the other when needed. That’s something Oregon hasn’t done this season, and I don’t expect them to on Saturday. Logan Brown: I’m so interested in this battle of the ground with Northwestern’s run game. They have a three-headed monster in the backfield, plus the mobility of quarterback Aidan Chiles. The Wildcats have run the ball so well this season, but it hasn’t always come easy on the road. Oregon has played the run better the past few weeks, but the Ducks couldn’t stop Illinois on the ground in the second half last week. If Northwestern runs the ball efficiently, they win with a huge advantage. If not, it can get interesting. Question: We've talked a lot about Oregon's offensive struggles, but the defense will have its hands full with Chip Kelly and a Northwestern offense that's been rolling this season. What's the biggest key for Oregon's defense to slow down the Wildcats and give the Ducks a chance to win? Zachary Neel: As I mentioned above, it's going to be all about slowing down the run for Northwestern. That means more than just Chiles, though. The Wildcats have a trio of very good running backs that can hurt you in different ways. If Northwestern is able to find success on the ground, it will open up the play-action passing game, where tight end Luke Dehnicke can be lethal. Bjorn Bergstrom: The biggest key is forcing Aidan Chiles to have an off day and revert back to his struggles from his first three seasons. During that time, Chiles was an erratic, turnover-prone passer lacking confidence. In 2026, he’s full of confidence and is an absolute baller, making plays that simply weren’t imaginable just 12 months ago. Getting in his face, making him feel pressure and not be able to get going with easy throws early is imperative for the Ducks. But with Kelly’s scheme, I lean towards Chiles being able to get going early. Logan Brown: I already talked about the run game, but the Ducks need to play disciplined against Chiles. The senior quarterback can burn them with RPO plays or just a regular read option. Northwestern utilizes the whole field with wide splits, so the pressure is on Oregon’s edge rushers more than ever to contain Chiles in the option and quick game and avoid getting caught too far up field. Gambling Corner Question: Gambling Corner: You get $100 to spread across the point spread (Oregon -3.5), and the Over/Under (47.5 points). How are you allocating your funds? Zachary Neel: Give me all $100 on Northwestern to cover. Vegas always knows something, but I don't know what in the world they've seen from the Ducks over the past month to consider them a 3.5-point favorite here. Bjorn Bergstrom: I think Northwestern will win, so I’m tempted to go there, but what in the world is pulling the over/under so high? Mehringer is gone but the bones of the offense are still here, along with a Ducks defense that has been dominant. I don’t see either team surpassing 24 points, so I’ll put all $100 on the under. Logan Brown: I’m putting $65 on Northwestern to cover the spread and the other $35 on the under. Northwestern’s offense is rolling right now, and Oregon’s is not, but I think both defenses could come to play on Saturday afternoon. Final Score Prediction Question: Who wins this game, and what is the final score? Zachary Neel: I've got Northwestern 27, Oregon 16. Bjorn Bergstrom: We’re about to see a Ducks team sitting at .500 as the calendar flips to November. Northwestern 20, Oregon 13. Logan Brown: Northwestern 24, Oregon 18. The Wildcats run the ball and grind the clock in the second half, and Oregon’s offense continues to struggle to find explosive plays. picks.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football takes on Northwestern
picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football takes on Northwestern Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 28, 2026, 8:52 a.m. PT Oregon's national-title hopes have ended after a loss to Illinois dropped them to 4-3. Oregon will face a one-loss Northwestern team featuring former Ducks coach Chip Kelly as offensive coordinator. The Ducks' defense is expected to play well, but the offense faces a tough challenge against Northwestern. The Oregon football team's national title hopes are all but over, and it isn't even November. After entering the season ranked as high as they've ever been, the Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) are unranked and out of the immediate College Football Playoff race after a stunning loss to Illinois on the road . The Ducks don't have much time to lick their wounds, either. After firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and announcing quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the 2026 season , one-loss Northwestern comes to town . Chip Kelly, who guided Oregon to a national championship game appearance as head coach over a decade ago, is the Wildcats' offensive coordinator. "It's almost like you're playing three different offenses," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said of Northwestern. "The new wrinkles that (Kelly) has at Northwestern, some of the old flavor that he has that he's carried all the way to his time back here at Oregon. There's always going to be something new when you walk into a game that it's going to be like he's never put this on film. He might not know how you're going to line up against it, and you have to figure it out there within the rules of your defense and how you execute." Oregon vs. Northwestern scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks will have the home crowd behind them in Eugene and also have deep familiarity with Northwestern's starting quarterback, Aidan Chiles. The senior signal-caller started his career at Oregon State before transferring to Michigan State in 2024. Chiles played at Autzen Stadium in that year and had a rough outing, completely just 10 of 17 passes for 154 yards in a 31-10 loss. The Ducks found ways to rattle Chiles early, and with a strong pass rush in recent weeks they could do so again Saturday. Why Northwestern has an advantage: The Wildcats, under first-year offensive coordinator and former Ducks coach Chip Kelly, have one of the most efficient offenses in the country and don't make many mistakes. Northwestern isn't necessarily an offensive juggernaut, but it ranks fifth in the country in turnover margin and moves the ball methodically while keeping opposing teams out of the end zone defensively. Though the Wildcats' defense gives up plenty of yards, they rank in the top 25 in scoring defense allowing just 16.6 points per game. Oregon vs. Northwestern injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: The Ducks will have a good chunk of playmakers returning to the sideline this weekend after sitting out last week due to unknown reasons. Evan Stewart, who was out last week after a DUII arrest, is expected back, as are Jalen Lott and Messiah Hampton. Lanning did not elaborate why Hampton and Lott missed last week. The coach also announced quarterback Dante Moore will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season after sustaining a concussion in late September. For Northwestern: The Wildcats were without several key contributors last week in a win against Rutgers, especially defensively. Second-leading tackler Robert Fitzgerald was held out, as well as defensive lineman Brendan Flakes. Oregon vs. Northwestern: 4 bold predictions Ducks will mostly contain vaunted Northwestern run game Though Chiles has been successful through the air in recent weeks, Northwestern's bread and butter is establishing the ground game. After a subpar performance stopping the run last week against Illinois, Oregon's defense will show up ready to play and stifle backs Caleb Komolafe, Joseph Himon II and Gavin Sawchuk. Outside of games versus Oklahoma State and Illinois, Oregon's run defense has been sound and it'll look like a motivated group against a physical Wildcats team this weekend. Gage Hurych will have a bounce-back performance vs. Wildcats After missing three field goals last week in a loss to Illinois, all from 40 yards or more, junior kicker Gage Hurych will have a strong game against Northwestern. The Wildcats give up a lot of yards with a bend-but-don't-break defense but are elite in the red zone, an area where Oregon's offense struggles. Northwestern opponents only score a touchdown on 40% of possessions that reach the red zone. If Oregon's offense stalls as it gets closer to the end zone, look for Hurych to have a bounce-back performance with more manageable field-goal attempts. Ducks' defense will keep them in it until the end Though Oregon's offense will likely still have trouble after firing Drew Mehringer, its defense will respond and keep them in the game until the fourth quarter. Outside of a couple of broken off runs in a loss to Illinois, the Ducks' defense has been one of the top units in the country over the last month and that will continue against Northwestern this weekend. It just won't be enough to get a win, unless the offense really corrects itself. Oregon football vs. Northwestern score prediction Northwestern 27, Oregon 16 Alec Dietz covers University of Oregon football and women’s basketball for The Register-Guard. The Gamecocks' success is primarily due to their rushing offense that averages an SEC-best 218.3 yards per game. It's been a combination of running back Matt Fuller and quarterback LaNorris Sellers on the ground. Fuller has 513 yards and five touchdowns. Sellers is right behind him with 507 yards and four touchdowns. The Sooners' offense is bogged down by its SEC-worst run game, but the passing game has also had its ups and downs. John Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards at a 66.7% completion rate with 11 touchdowns to seven interceptions, tied for the second most in the SEC. Wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III has the sixth-most receiving yards in the SEC with 578 and three touchdowns Although the Sooners have faced plenty of challenges offensively, their defense has played well, ranking second in the SEC in total yards allowed and first in pass defense. Part of their ability to defend well against the pass is their pass rush that's gotten 22 sacks, which ties for third in the SEC. South Carolina vs Oklahoma scouting report Why South Carolina has an advantage: Even though Oklahoma's defense is its strength, against the run, the Sooners haven't been as formidable as they are against the pass. They allow an average of 117.4 rushing yards, ranking eighth in the SEC. This favors a South Carolina team that gains most of its yards on the ground. As for facing the Sooners' pressure on passing plays, the Gamecocks' offensive line has held its own, allowing 15 sacks, tied for sixth in the SEC. Sellers' mobility will also be an asset in allowing him to escape the pocket and break free on scrambles, in addition to his designed runs. Why Oklahoma has an advantage: The Sooners have struggled to score but now face a bottom-five SEC defense in points allowed. Mateer could have an easier time settling into a rhythm against the Gamecocks, who give up 222.7 passing yards per game and have just four interceptions. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers put together a great 2024 campaign before struggling for most of last season and at the start of this year. But he showed off his freakish athleticism Saturday against the Volunteers with one of the most impressive 4-yard gains for a touchdown you'll see. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is a big-play threat at any moment. Defensively, Dylan Stewart wreaks havoc on most offenses he faces — he's recorded two sacks and forced three fumbles in four games this season. The case for South Carolina: Beamer has the Gamecocks rolling. Momentum can be a real thing. If Sellers limits his turnovers and South Carolina's defense forces OU quarterback John Mateer, it'll have a good chance on the road. If the Sooners can continue their upward trajectory against the Gamecocks, they'll have a chance. If not - if John Mateer has to lead the team in rushing attempts and the Sooners average less than 4 yards per carry, then desperation will set in, Mateer will be forced to make plays - then bad things will happen. But if OU can run the ball just a little, Mateer can relax and guys like Isaiah Sategna and Rocky Beers and Lloyd Avant can help out the defense by moving the chains, changing the scoreboard and winning a home game. Final: Oklahoma 21, South Carolina 13 John Mateer found a healthy headspace in Starkville, but Saturday will be the first real test to see if he can stick to the plan. South Carolina's defense is not impenetrable, but it's a much better group than Mississippi State's, with difference-makers who can wreck drives and put Mateer into tough situations. It's likely there will be a turnover, and the test will be if OU's quarterback can rebound after that. History says he'll have a tough time. Brent Venables' defense will get its third look at talented quarterback LaNorris Sellers, but if Oklahoma is unable to finish off drives, the Gamecocks have shown they can notch dramatic victories. Final: South Carolina 20, Oklahoma 13 Someone from the future could tell me a plethora of different outcomes from Saturday's game, and I'd believe them. Oklahoma's offense certainly made progress against Mississippi State, and it's possible that the Sooners build on those improvements at home against South Carolina. But it also wouldn't be shocking if OU's offense regressed into the turnover-prone unit that it was against Kentucky, Georgia, New Mexico and Michigan. South Carolina comes into Norman on a two-game winning streak after ranked victories over Florida (on the road) and Tennessee - the Gamecocks seem like they're due for a letdown. While South Carolina's defense is better than Mississippi State's was, there are plenty of areas for the Sooners to expose, assuming they can play a similarly clean game on Saturday. Oklahoma needs a win to stay above .500, and I expect the Sooners to earn a close victory over the Gamecocks. Final: Oklahoma 20, South Carolina 17 The Gamecocks are more dangerous than Mississippi State, on both sides of the ball. Last week was a small step forward for the Sooners' offense, nota giant leap. Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't completely fixed just because he had a solid game against the Bulldogs. But with Michael Fasusi back on the offensive line, the Sooners' offense adds layers. They don't have to have every element working in order to be successful. What they do need to do, though, is protect the football and keep up their strong defensive play. This game will be back and forth and figures to go down to the wire, but in the end, Oklahoma does just enough to start its first winning streak of the season. Brady Trantham The 2026 season is still up in the air. One thing it has told us is that basically no one has been able to handle a big emotional win and follow that up with another win a week later. South Carolina's win over Tennessee was very much an emotional win against a highly-ranked opponent - the Volunteers themselves had just beaten Alabama the week prior. OU has slowly built consistency on offense, just enough that paired with an elite defense, victories against flawed teams are realistic. The Sooners have proven to be great at corralling mobile quarterbacks and will showcase that again, while John Mateer will build off a great performance last week against a dangerous but very gettable defense. (Sam Wolfe/Special To The State) Michael Sauls Thu, October 29, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads South Carolina football is hitting the road this weekend. Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks will travel to Norman, Oklahoma, on Saturday to face Brent Venables and the Oklahoma Sooners. The SEC matchup is set to kick off at 4:15 and will be televised on SEC Network. South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) is coming off a big win over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week. Oklahoma beat Mississippi State last week on the road. The Gamecocks and Sooners have played just twice in the all-time series. South Carolina beat Oklahoma on the road in 2024 and the Sooners beat the Gamecocks last year in Columbia. Here's what you need to know about Saturday's game: Is South Carolina vs. Oklahoma football game on TV? Who: South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) vs. Oklahoma (4-3, 2-3 SEC) When: Saturday, Oct. 31 at 4:15 p.m. Where : Memorial Stadium in Norman, Oklahoma Watch: SEC Network Stream: ESPN app or ESPN.com Broadcast crew: Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik, Michella Chester Local radio crew: Todd Ellis, Tommy Suggs, Chet Tucker Satellite radio: Sirius XM Channel 176 or 229 (953 on app) Series history: Tied 1-1 (Oklahoma won last matchup in 2025) South Carolina vs. Oklahoma betting odds Despite pulling off back-to-back ranked upsets, and being favored over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week, South Carolina is an underdog this week. Oklahoma opened as a 5.5-point favorite, according to the VegasInsider consensus . That line has since moved a bit and the Sooners are now favored by 4.5 points by major sportsbooks such as FanDuel and DraftKings. South Carolina is 3-4 against the spread this year. ESPN Analytics also favors the Sooners. ESPN gives South Carolina a 36.1% chance of winning the game. Injury updates South Carolina had seven players listed on the official SEC injury report released Wednesday night. WR Jayden Sellers, edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josian Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. Sellers and Thompson are both out for the year. DB Quay'sheed Scott and RB Jawarn Howell are both listed as doubtful. Scott has missed the last two games. Howell was out last week vs. Tennessee. The SEC injury report will be updated on Thursday, Friday and 90 minutes before kickoff on Saturday. Weather forecast for the game in Norman If you're making the trip to Oklahoma this weekend, be sure to pack an umbrella and a jacket. Temperatures aren't expected to surpass 64 degrees and will dip into the mid-50s. There will be thick cloud cover with a touch of rain, per Accuweather's 10-day forecast. There's a 55% chance of rain all day Saturday for the Norman area. Top storylines Three's a streak: A win over Oklahoma on Saturday would give South Carolina its third straight win. The Gamecocks haven't won three consecutive SEC games since they ended the 2024 season with four straight SEC wins. That six-game winning streak to close out the 2024 season was also the last time the Gamecocks won three games in a row. Should USC beat Oklahoma, it would get the Gamecocks' SEC record back to .500. Sellers needs help in the run game: Make no mistake, South Carolina still has the No. 1 rushing offense in the SEC. The Gamecocks are averaging 218 yards per game, but things haven't looked perfect in recent weeks. Anyone not named LaNorris Sellers has had trouble consistently running the ball for South Carolina. Sellers has accounted for 313 of the 480 rushing yards the Gamecocks have compiled in the last three games. That's certainly good, but USC's running backs need to get going so all the pressure isn't on Sellers' legs down the stretch. Ranking on the horizon? South Carolina received votes in both the Associated Press Top 25 and USA Today Coaches Poll this week after beating Tennessee. USC received 12 votes from the coaches and eight votes from the media. Will a win over Oklahoma be enough to catapult USC into the national rankings for the first time since September 2025? Only time will tell. South Carolina and Oklahoma players to watch South Carolina K Malik Orsan: The sophomore was South Carolina's savior last week. Orsan drilled a 48-yard field goal to help the Gamecocks beat then-No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 as the clock expired. The Southeast Missouri State transfer wasn't necessarily considered to be the top kicker on the roster during USC's kicking competition this offseason. But he's quickly proven why he won the starting job by going 10 for 12 on field goal attempts and 22 for 22 on extra-point attempts this season. South Carolina OL Nolan Hay: The fifth-year offensive lineman was named the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week on Tuesday by the Football Writers Association of America. Hay has been one of the best offensive linemen for the Gamecocks this year. He typically starts at guard but has played some center in Carter Miller's absence because of injury. Hay's Pro Football Focus blocking grade is one of the best on the team. Oklahoma QB John Mateer: There was some buzz around Mateer's name this offseason, but he's found himself in a bit of a rut in 2026. Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards and 11 touchdowns but has also thrown seven interceptions. He's got a strong arm and is capable of using his legs in the ground game, but has been generally turnover-prone this season. Oklahoma WR Isaiah Sategna III: Sategna was an All-SEC player last year after finishing with 965 receiving yards. The fifth-year student has been Mateer's favorite target in 2026. Sategna leads Oklahoma with 41 catches and 578 yards.

picks.headline: Oklahoma Sooners Football vs. South Carolina Game Preview, Notes, Odds and Broadcast Info
picks.blurb: Oklahoma Sooners Football vs. South Carolina Game Preview, Notes, Odds and Broadcast Info - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em (Jeff Blake-Imagn Images) Tyler Jones Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:09 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Game Information - NR/RV Oklahoma (4-3, 2-2 SEC) vs. RV/RV South Carolina (4-3, 2-3) - Start Time: 3:15 p.m. CT - Location: Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium, Norman, OK - Odds: Oklahoma -3.5 (O/U 44.5) If you or someone you know has a gambling problem, call 1-800-GAMBLER. The National Council on Problem Gambling help line is also often cited at 1-800-522-4700. Broadcast Details - TV: SEC Network and ESPN Unlimited (Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik and Michella Chester) - Radio: Sooner Sports Network via 107.7 The Franchise/KOKC 95.3 and 1520 in Oklahoma City, 1430 The Buzz/KMOD 97.5 in Tulsa, and on The Varsity Network app (Toby Rowland, Teddy Lehman, Chris Plank, and Gabe Ikard) What You Need To Know NORMAN, Okla. — Oklahoma's season has refused to settle into anything comfortable. Saturday's homecoming game against South Carolina is the next chance to stop the bouncing. The Sooners are 4-3 and 2-2 in the SEC heading into a 3:15 p.m. kickoff at Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. South Carolina arrives at 4-3 and 2-3, receiving votes, and playing with the confidence of a team that just knocked off Florida and Tennessee. That alone should wipe out any idea that this is a soft home date. The Gamecocks have already shown they can travel, finish close games, and lean on a quarterback who creates problems Oklahoma has to solve with discipline more than highlight-hunt pressure. There is history all over this one too. Shane Beamer spent 2018 through 2020 in Norman as Oklahoma's assistant head coach on offense, working tight ends and H-backs during a 33-6 stretch that included three Big 12 titles and two College Football Playoff appearances. Brent Venables, meanwhile, spent years tormenting South Carolina from the Clemson sideline. He went 7-2 against the Gamecocks as defensive coordinator and held them to 14.9 points per game in those seven wins. The recent series between these two programs has swung hard both ways: South Carolina won 35-9 in Norman in 2024 after Oklahoma turned it over on its first three possessions, then the Sooners answered with a 26-7 road win last year by smothering the Gamecocks and winning the line of scrimmage. That 2024 home loss is still the warning label. Oklahoma actually outgained South Carolina that day and held them to 69 second-half yards. It did not matter. Four turnovers and a 24-0 deficit in points off turnovers decided the afternoon before the Sooners ever found their footing. That has been the split-screen identity of this entire season too. In the wins over Texas and Mississippi State, Oklahoma had four takeaways and only one giveaway. In the losses to Georgia and Kentucky, it had two takeaways and eight giveaways. When the Sooners protect the ball, they look like a team that can still climb. When they do not, the defense gets asked to cover for a mess it did not create. The weirdest layer is the pattern. Oklahoma has followed every win with a loss and every loss with a win through seven games, the first time in program history the Sooners have alternated results across the first seven contests. If that pattern holds, homecoming would be a loss. That is exactly the kind of empty narrative this team needs to bury. South Carolina is the seventh straight opponent that was ranked or receiving votes at kickoff. The schedule has not given Oklahoma many clean emotional resets. This is another one that will have heat on it from the start. Oklahoma's defense remains the reason this team is still interesting. The Sooners lead the nation in first downs allowed per game and sit among the national leaders in third-down defense, red-zone defense, pass defense, sacks, and total defense. Opponents have scored on just 23 percent of their possessions. All 14 defensive starters began their college careers at Oklahoma. Owen Heinecke continues to lead the team in tackles and has become the week-to-week constant at linebacker. The front still has enough disruption to wreck drives when the edges stay clean. South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers is built to test that cleanliness. He is a big, physical quarterback who can push the ball downfield and punish soft contain with his legs. He has already thrown for more than 1,500 yards and added over 500 on the ground. The Gamecocks' recent upswing has come with far better ball security and enough confidence to finish against ranked teams. If Oklahoma's edge players get greedy or abandon lanes, Sellers can turn ordinary scrambles into drive-extending runs. The Sooners need a cage-rush approach more than a free-for-all. Squeeze the pocket, stay in assignment, and make him beat the structure with processing instead of freelancing into open space. Peyton Bowen's status adds some stress on the back end. He has been one of Oklahoma's most important defensive players all season, with takeaways that directly turned into points against Texas and Mississippi State. He is also coming out of the Mississippi State game dealing with a leg/stinger issue. If he is limited, somebody else has to clean up the explosive answers and help finish when Sellers extends plays. South Carolina's best chance is not a perfect 12-play drive script. It is one broken containment snap and one missed tackle in space. John Mateer's Starkville tape is the first real reset of the year at quarterback. He completed 22 of 29 passes for 283 yards and two touchdowns, did not throw an interception, and helped Oklahoma post season highs in total offense and rushing in a road win. Isaiah Sategna went off for 164 yards. Rocky Beers stayed productive. The run game finally had some weight to it, including a long run from Tory Blaylock that flipped the third quarter. Venables has already said that version of Mateer is what Oklahoma needs the rest of the way. That has to show up again Saturday. Mateer is at 1,591 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and seven interceptions on the season. The efficiency can play. The turnover number is still the ceiling-cutter. South Carolina will give him enough looks to get comfortable if he stays patient and uses Beers as the safety valve while Sategna works the intermediate and deep parts of the field. Beers has been one of the better transfer additions in the league and continues to lead SEC tight ends in receiving yards per game. Sategna remains the explosive piece defenses have to account for every series. The offensive line remains the quieter concern. Availability has been uneven all season, and Oklahoma has had to patch together combinations on the fly. Against a South Carolina front that will try to clutter lanes and force Mateer into longer holds, that matters. The Sooners do not need 500 yards again. They need manageable downs, fewer empty possessions, and enough balance to keep Sellers' offense from owning the tempo of the day. There is a temptation to overstate every remaining game because the margin is already thin. Fair enough. ESPN's FPI has Oklahoma projected around the 6-6 range, and the remaining stretch still includes Florida, Ole Miss, Texas A&M, and Missouri. That means Saturday is not just another home date. It is one of the clearer opportunities to create breathing room. A win over South Carolina would make Oklahoma 5-3 and 3-2, with some actual traction in league play. It would also reinforce the only formula that has worked this year: defense travels, takeaways matter, and the quarterback has to stop donating points. A loss would push the Sooners back into the same uneasy place they occupied after Kentucky, with the season again asking whether the good nights are sustainable or just occasional interruptions. South Carolina is not an unknown. Beamer knows Norman. Sellers can take over a game if Oklahoma gets careless. The Gamecocks are playing better now than they were in September. All of that is true. It is also true that Oklahoma can win this game if it plays like the team that handled Texas and Mississippi State instead of the one that buried itself in turnovers against Georgia and Kentucky. Homecoming should not require a miracle. It requires cleanliness. Keep Sellers crowded. Make South Carolina drive the hard way. Let Mateer play the next snap instead of the last mistake. If the Sooners do that, Norman should still be a hard place to leave with a win. If they do not, the pattern everyone is already talking about will get one more chapter.

away.headline: South Carolina vs. Oklahoma injury report: Jawarn Howell, Quay'Sheed Scott ruled out
away.blurb: On Thursday evening, just two days before the Gamecocks are set to kick off, South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer announced that Gamecock running back Jawarn Howell and defensive back Quay'Sheed Scott will both be out for Saturday's game. Coach Beamer gave the update during his weekly radio show, stating that both guys will be out for the game against the Sooners. “It will say that ‘Sheed is out again this week,” Beamer said via Gamecock Central. “He’s got some tests that have to get done tomorrow, and we’re optimistic on what those test will say, and if they say what we hope it’s going to say, he’ll be playing next week against Texas A&M. Jawarn won’t play Saturday; he banged his shoulder up, I guess Wednesday, in practice last week or maybe it was Friday, but late in the week. He was available last week in the Tennessee game, just has still been bothering him, and we thought the best thing for him was just still to be able to rest that shoulder a little bit this week and get that healthy. So those two are out.” Scott has not played since South Carolina's Oct. 3 game at home against the Kentucky Wildcats. The Gamecocks starting nickelback left the game and did not return, even having to be hospitalized as a precaution. Coach Beamer has not disclosed the specifics regarding his injury. Howell has also missed time this season with an injury, as he did not play in last week's win over Tennessee. Although his status changed from doubtful to questionable throughout the week last week ahead of the game against the Vols, he was ruled out and did not play. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. home.headline: South Carolina vs. Oklahoma injury report: Jawarn Howell, Quay'Sheed Scott ruled out
home.blurb: On Thursday evening, just two days before the Gamecocks are set to kick off, South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer announced that Gamecock running back Jawarn Howell and defensive back Quay'Sheed Scott will both be out for Saturday's game. Coach Beamer gave the update during his weekly radio show, stating that both guys will be out for the game against the Sooners. “It will say that ‘Sheed is out again this week,” Beamer said via Gamecock Central. “He’s got some tests that have to get done tomorrow, and we’re optimistic on what those test will say, and if they say what we hope it’s going to say, he’ll be playing next week against Texas A&M. Jawarn won’t play Saturday; he banged his shoulder up, I guess Wednesday, in practice last week or maybe it was Friday, but late in the week. He was available last week in the Tennessee game, just has still been bothering him, and we thought the best thing for him was just still to be able to rest that shoulder a little bit this week and get that healthy. So those two are out.” Scott has not played since South Carolina's Oct. 3 game at home against the Kentucky Wildcats. The Gamecocks starting nickelback left the game and did not return, even having to be hospitalized as a precaution. Coach Beamer has not disclosed the specifics regarding his injury. Howell has also missed time this season with an injury, as he did not play in last week's win over Tennessee. Although his status changed from doubtful to questionable throughout the week last week ahead of the game against the Vols, he was ruled out and did not play. It may have only counted as one defeat on the ledger, but it really did feel like 2.5 losses mentally. For better or worse, the Tigers must turn the page and get ready for potentially a wild road game at the rival Florida State Seminoles. It will be during Halloween, nevertheless, so get ready for it. Clemson enters play at 4-3 on the season and 2-2 in the ACC. It has wins over Georgia Southern, North Carolina, Cal, and Charleston Southern, with losses to LSU, Miami, and Virginia Tech. While Florida State is only 3-4 on the season, Mike Norvell's Seminoles have a knack for scoring points and playing some fairly competitive football at home. Dabo Swinney cannot let his team overlook FSU. With that all in mind, here are the latest betting odds, how to watch this game, and a game prediction. Latest betting odds for Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles According to the FanDuel Sportsbook , Florida State will be laying 5.5 points to visiting Clemson. The associated moneylines for this game are Florida State -215 and Clemson +180. This means that it would take a $215 bet on Florida State to win $100, while wagering $100 on Clemson would pocket you $180. The projected point total for the game comes in at a combined 49.5 points, down from 51.5. Using all of that information above, a projected final score for this game would be something in the vicinity of Florida State 27.5, Clemson 22. While the odds for this game have fluctuated a bit , Florida State has been the favorite throughout for two reasons. It is a home game for the Seminoles, and the meager Tigers' offense has struggled to score points against Power Four competition all season long. You are not going to want to miss this rivalry game! Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles game prediction This high-stakes ACC rivalry game will come down to one of two things. From the Florida State perspective, it will be all about how disciplined the Seminoles' pass defense will be. This team can score points, but it does love to give them up in bunches. As for Clemson, the Tigers need to show on offense that they can put up 30 or so points if they need to get into some sort of a low-end shootout. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Will the Tigers' run of dominance in the rivalry continue or end Saturday in Tallahassee? Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Florida State as a 6.5-point favorite over Clemson, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, doesn't favor the Tigers, either. It gives Florida State a 71.9% chance to win and Clemson a 28.1% chance. The Tigers are 51st nationally in ESPN's FPI with a 5.8 rating, which ranks 11th among the 17 ACC teams. Florida State has a 10.1 FPI rating that's 37th nationally. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Kansas State (5.7) and one spot below Virginia (6.0). Clemson football odds of reaching bowl game after brutal Week 7 loss to Virginia Tech In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 78.1%, down from 88.4% prior to its loss to Virginia Tech. Clemson's chances of winning its final five games are just 2.1%, according to ESPN's FPI. FPI represents how many points above or below average a team is. Projected results are based on 20,000 simulations of the rest of the season using FPI, results to date, and the remaining schedule. Ratings and projections update daily. FPI data from seasons prior to 2019 may not be complete." picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Clemson Tigers | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 30, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football FSU looks to get to .500 and avoid 3rd straight loss as home favorites The Florida State Seminoles will host the Clemson Tigers this Saturday for a Halloween evening rivalry game at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee. The kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m., and the game will be televised by the ACCN. This will be the 39th meeting between the teams, with Florida State (3-4, 1-3 ACC) leading the all-time series 21-17, including a 12-7 record at Doak and an 18-15 record as ACC members. However, Clemson has won the last two meetings and holds a 15-7 advantage over the last 22 games, including wins in nine of the last 10 meetings. Clemson will be attempting to win a fifth consecutive game at Doak, becoming only the third program ever to win five consecutive road games against FSU in Tallahassee, joining Florida (six straight from 1966-76) and Miami (Fla.) (five from 1957-77). Despite Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State combining for 13 of the last 15 ACC championships, both teams are struggling this year. Clemson’s losses have come against #15 LSU, #1 Miami, and a 6-2 Virginia Tech team that scored the winning touchdown with 1:44 left on the clock. FSU’s four losses were in double overtime at #1 Miami, at #10 Alabama, at home against #19 SMU, and at Louisville when the defense totally collapsed. Clemson’s defense is the strength of their team. The Tigers rank 32nd in total defense (317), 36th in passing (186), T-53rd in rushing defense (131), T-30th in third-down defense (holding opponents to a 33.3-percent conversion rate), have allowed only four passing touchdowns, and have recorded 20 sacks through seven games. The Tigers’ passing offense, behind true freshman QB Tait Reynolds, who was named starter following an injury to Christopher Vizzina in their 2nd game, has only thrown one touchdown, and the 2 QBs combined have only thrown 2 TDs all season. Reynolds has been sacked 20 times this season and has thrown 3 interceptions while averaging just 6.1 yards per completion. Overall, Clemson has allowed 21 sacks, rank 115th in total offense (333). 112th in scoring offense, 115th in passing offense, 126th in 3rd-down conversion (31.7%), and 93rd in red zone offense. Florida State looks to avoid its 3rd straight loss after a heartbreaking double-overtime loss to Miami. The Noles were able to rush for 138 yards against the nation’s #1-ranked rushing defense; however, leading rusher Ousmane Kromah sustained a lower-leg injury and will miss the rest of the 2026 season. FSU loses double-overtime heartbreaker to Miami Social media reactions to the end of FSU vs. Miami Column: ACC replay review never entertained another outcome on FSU’s final play FSU running back Ousmane Kromah carted off near the end of first half against Miami Despite having a losing season record, FSU’s offense is ranked T-49th in the nation in total offense, 50th in scoring, 46th in rushing, 63rd in passing, and 34th in red-zone offense. FSU individual leaders After allowing Miami to rack up 583 total yards on 78 plays for a 7.5 yard average/play, FSU’s defense now ranks 130th in the nation, giving up 435 yards/game, 124th in passing defense (256 yards/game), T-112th in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert nearly 43% of the time on third-down attempts, and T-104th in first-down defense, allowing their opponents 155 first downs (22.1/game) in the 7 games played this season. Florida State is currently trending as a 5.5-point favorite with the over/under set at 49.5 points, according to FanDuel. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Clemson Tigers Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Jordan Silversmith (season record: 6-1) This game is a tricky one to call. I do not think Clemson is a good football team. However, they probably have the best unit on the field: their defense. Another issue for Florida State is that the Seminoles have historically struggled against the Tigers, with no home wins in the last decade. Even so, FSU should win on Saturday night. I imagine that, off a bye, head coach Mike Norvell will scheme up points on the opening drive, and Tony White’s defense should make forcing CU to throw the name of the game. This game will be close, as it often is with FSU, but Clemson isn’t good enough right now to win a rivalry game on the road. Seminole win, but no cover. FSU 27, Clemson 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 6-1) This could be a scary game, fitting for Halloween. With Kromah out, Clemson’s defense may keep FSU in check but the Tiger’s offense is dreadful. If Clemson somehow overwhelm’s Tony White’s defense, that relationship needs to end. I think FSU wins but it will be ugly. FSU 24, Clemson 17 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-2 ) Call me crazy, but this game is going to be completely unwatchable but FSU will emerge victorious. Firstly, it’s at Doak. On Halloween. Where else would you rather be? In all seriousness, Clemson’s offensive efficiency is dreadful. Like, REALLY dreadful. Per Game On Paper , Clemson’s EPA per pass is #136 out of #138 and their EPA per rush is #110. They are only 33.7% successful on third down, good for #128, and they are just bad at most things offense, mainly because their QB is a freshman. Their defense is good to great, though! #13 in EPA/Pass defense and just middle of the pack on rushing defense, #64 in the nation. Florida State meanwhile… their defense is trash. #127 on EPA per pass, #105 on EPA per rush, #120 on 3rd/4th down stops. The offense is good, though. #39 in EPA/Pass, #36 in EPA/Rush. If they can handle Clemson’s terrible offense and do good things on defense against a very not good Clemson offense, it might be a fun halloweekend in Tallahassee. Give me the Noles to pull off, not an upset per se, just a good, scrappy win. Florida State 14, Clemson 13 Curt Weiler (season record: 5-2, 2-5 ATS) Call me crazy for buying in again but I think I believe in this FSU team more than I do that Clemson team. The Tigers’ defense is pretty good. But the offense is very bad. Clemson is the only FBS team which has scored more points from its defense/special teams than its offense . To Tony White and his unit, I would say “If not now, when?” FSU 27, Clemson 20 NoleThruandThru (season record: 7-0) I’m taking a break from the Marshawn gag this week to honor my dad, who passed away two weeks ago. The world lost a wonderful FSU alum and fan, and I hope he enjoys this one from heaven. FSU 28, Clemson 24 Jon Marchant (season record: 6-1 ) Nobody knows what kind of team FSU will be from week to week. No result is off the table and there’s no score that would surprise anyone. So I’m picking FSU this week. Just cause. Also, it’s funny when Dabo loses. Clemson 23, FSU 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 5-1) I’m picking FSU but I don’t feel great about the prediction. I’m really worried about what FSU’s offense will look like without Kromah vs. Clemson’s defense. That being said I have not seen enough from Clemson’s offense to stay off the field and if you give FSU’s skill group enough shots they’re going to get points. Noles win. FSU 24 Clemson 17 Matt Minnick (Season record: 5-2; ATS: 4-3) As others have said, Clemson’s offense is putrid. Two passing touchdowns all season long is nearly unfathomable. But is Tony White’s defense just what the doctor ordered? It’s the moveable object vs the stoppable force. I’ve said all year that despite all the suckage over the last three seasons, FSU has honestly been pretty decent at home. However, Norvell’s teams also have a penchant for finding ways to lose very winnable games. If Kromah was healthy, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If Quindarious Jones was healthy I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If a random FCS DC who’s name was drawn out of a hat was FSU’s defensive coordinator, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. Clemson 30 , FSU 28 Frank DNole (season record: 3-4) FSU’s offense is better than Clemson’s defense. Clemson’s offense is about as good as FSU’s defense. Advantage Noles. This will be the game that turns the program around, and everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are 5.5-point favorites for a reason. Vegas knows something and the Seminoles know it too. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed against Virginia. The Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their equally talented Clempsun opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, Orange Dabo’s 27 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 4-3, 3-4 ATS) For all its flaws over the last two seasons, FSU has taken care of business against the teams it should beat while in the confines of Doak. I have faith in FSU’s ability to get enough points against a stout Clemson defense and, as naive as it might be, take care of business against a dreadful Tigers offense. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State (3-4, 1-3), which have played every year since 1992 with the exception of 2020, are both at a crossroads. Neither program wants to move on from its coach and pay a hefty buyout, but neither team has shown very much on the field lately to offer hope. The Tigers suffered a 20-16 gut-punch loss to Virginia Tech in Week 8. It marked Clemson's eighth in its last 10 games against a Power Four opponent at home. The Tigers led for much of the second half until Ethan Grunkemeyer's game-winning 5-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-1 with 1:44 left. Florida State came within a play or two of adding to the chaos that was college football's thrilling Week 7 slate. The Seminoles took Miami to double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium. FSU quarterback Ashton Daniels accounted for five touchdowns in the loss, including four through the air. Clemson hasn't thrown four touchdowns all season. Tait Reynolds, the 19-year-old true freshman who was thrust into the starting job following an injury to Christopher Vizzina, is averaging just 6.1 yards per completion and has been sacked 20 times in seven games behind a weak offensive line. Clemson ranks 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game, which is last in the ACC. Florida State ranks 49th with 414.3 total yards per games. Here's ESPN's prediction for Saturday's game. Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Florida State, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Seminoles winning their first game against the Tigers at Doak Campbell Stadium since 2014. The oddsmakers' latest 5.5 spread favors FSU, as well. Connelly's final score prediction: Florida State 27, Clemson 24. He gives the Seminoles a win probability of 59%. Where Clemson, Florida State sit in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 9 rivalry Clemson is No. 55 in ESPN's SP+ team rankings , up one spot from last week despite the loss to Virginia Tech. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.7, up from 4.0 a week ago. Clemson is one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's overall team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.3 rating on offense (No. 97 nationally, up one spot from last week) and a 19.0 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is the same as before the Tigers' loss to the Hokies. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.5 rating, which ranks 10th-best in the nation. Florida State is No. 54 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 5.8, one spot below Virginia and one ahead of Clemson. The metrics give the Seminoles a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 32 nationally, a 27.1 rating on defense that's No. 76, and a 0.2 rating in special teams that's 43rd in the country. What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. The game can be seen on ACC Network. Wes Durham and Max Browne will have the call of the game. Madison Fitzpatrick will report from the sidelines. The Clemson Athletic Network feed of the game featuring Tigers radio play-by-play voice Don Munson and analysts Tim Bourret and Jeff Scott can be heard on SiriusXM channel 258. away.blurb: Florida State starting cornerback Quindarrius Jones is listed as out on the injury report Oct. 29 for Clemson football 's game against FSU. Jones missed two games earlier this season against Central Arkansas and Alabama, but returned to play Virginia, Louisville and Miami. However, Jones is now out again. Elsewhere on FSU's injury report is leading rusher Ousmane Kromah, who suffered a season-ending fracture and dislocation in his left ankle against Miami on Oct. 17 and is listed as out. Starting linebacker Chris Jones, the Seminoles' leading tackler, is still listed as probable. Starting linebacker Omar Graham Jr. was removed from the injury report. On Clemson 's end, backup wide receiver Gordon Sellars III (concussion) is listed as questionable. away.blurb: Florida State and Clemson released their initial availability reports on Wednesday night. At that time, the two teams ruled out a combined 16 players. Florida State downgraded senior safety K.J. Kirkland from questionable to doubtful. The Seminoles will likely have to rely on their depth in the back end once again, with senior cornerback Quindarrius Jones already ruled out. On the positive side, fifth-year linebackers Mikai Gbayor and Omar Graham Jr., along with junior quarterback Malachi Marshall are no longer on the report. That basically means they were upgraded from probable to available. While the matchup against the Clemson Tigers may not rise to the magnitude of the Florida Gators or Miami Hurricanes, it's traditionally been one of the most important annual games in the ACC. Neither team was above .500 last year, and it's not much better in 2026. Clemson is 4-3, and Florida State is 3-4. home.headline: Devin Carter's return is huge, but Florida State still needs to answer a bigger question
home.blurb: Norvell did not provide specifics or explain just how much the Seminoles' staff plans on utilizing Carter, but his return to the field comes at a key time. Florida State has a completely decimated backfield and an offense that is desperate to find playmakers at any position. Help is truly needed, and a healthy Carter might be able to do so, but now the question is whether or not that impact will be felt against Clemson. With limited options left on offense, Florida State is going to have to change a few things around against Clemson, starting with how the team attacks. Ousmane Kromah and Samuel Singleton Jr. are both out, meaning the team is down to just three healthy running backs, including two who have barely played at the collegiate level. Nobody in the receiving room has truly stepped up this season consistently, and that is a problem that the Seminoles need to shake without either starting running back available. Wide receiver Devin Carter is coming off the injury report for the first time this season, and the receiver is expected to make his collegiate debut against Clemson. Can Devin Carter help Florida State solve some of the issues on offense through the air? No shade to Amari Thomas or Tre Wisner at all, but replicating the consistency and success of Ousmane Kromah is difficult to do, even with two players. Kromah's value to the team is immense, and Florida State's run game will certainly take a hit without his leadership in the backfield. Something has got to give, and either Florida State finds ways to attack through the air or the team sends Thomas and Wisner straight into walls of defenders. This is where Carter comes into play, as a fresh new receiver who was exciting throughout camp, making plays that even the experienced receivers struggled to make. It is hard to imagine Carter triumphing in his collegiate debut, but Florida State needs someone to take the lead, and the freshman has all of the tools to do so. Part of the issues Florida State has had through the air this season can be attributed to quarterback Ashton Daniels, who struggles at times to accurately push the football through the air. However, another problem has been the fact that Daniels rarely has an open look by the time he needs to get rid of the football. home.headline: Florida State injury updates: Mike Norvell expects key returns, but timing is an issue
home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Miami looks to stay unbeaten against a sneaky-good North Carolina team on the road Getty Images Prior to last week, Miami had not held the No. 1 spot in the AP Top 25 poll since 2002, but so far the Hurricanes are looking every bit the part of the best team in the country. Not only have they raced out to a 7-0 start this year, but they've done so in a way that suggests a continuation of the success that led Miami all the way to the national championship game last season. With a 14-1 record in its last 15 games, Miami has been one of the best teams in the country since early November 2025, and now each week provides yet another opportunity for this year's team to validate that high poll ranking. This week, that means a trip to Chapel Hill to take on Bill Belichick and North Carolina in a game that offers Cristobal and Miami a chance to reverse a recent skid in the series. The Tar Heels have won their last five meetings in the series, including a 2-0 record against Cristobal with wins in 2022 and 2023. But those two Miami teams finished a combined 12-13 overall, while this year's group is clearly playing on a different level. For starters, those teams didn't have not just one but two Heisman Trophy contenders like Miami does this year with quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney . Those last teams that lost to North Carolina also didn't carry the nation's best scoring margin, as Miami does currently, beating opponents by 33.7 points per game. There's some history that favors UNC, sure, but Miami's strength will challenge the impact of the past. Miami vs. North Carolina: Need to know Tar Heels looking to bounce back from upset home loss: While Miami validated its position at No. 1 last week with a thorough thrashing of Pitt, North Carolina saw some of the hype for this matchup cooled by an upset loss at home to Syracuse . The Tar Heels led by 10 points in the fourth quarter but let Steve Angeli and the Orange offense back into the game with a couple late scores before eventually falling in overtime. That's brought even more urgency to Bill Belichick's crew to have their game locked in for Saturday night, because the kind of failure at the margins that led to the fourth-quarter collapse will only be exposed more dramatically against a team of Miami's caliber. The Tar Heels have shown in wins over TCU , Pitt and Duke that they can play a tight game and come out on the right side of close margins, but those victories (and certainly any upset effort against Miami) require a cleaner effort than North Carolina showed against Syracuse last week. A Saturday showcase spot for Miami's Heisman Trophy contenders: Miami has a nice two-week run where its opponents and the stage will allow for quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney to receive a big-time spotlight in the national conversation. This week's game against North Carolina, on Halloween night in Chapel Hill, will draw plenty of attention and could allow the Hurricanes (who are 14-point favorites) to continue building the resumes of both Mensah and Toney. Mensah is putting together one of the best starts to a season we have seen from a quarterback this century, currently leading the nation in completion percentage (81.4%) while also rolling up 22 passing touchdowns (2nd in FBS) and 307.3 passing yards per game (fourth in FBS). Malachi Toney, meanwhile, leads the FBS in receptions (66) and has become the first wide receiver with at least 900 receiving yards and 10 receiving touchdowns on a 7-0 team since eventual Heisman winner DeVonta Smith in 2020. Miami is elite in the middle (of games): It's easy to look at the collection of talent Mario Cristobal has assembled as an explanation for the team's dominance, but that talent has to perform to deliver the kind of results the Hurricanes have been getting over the last two seasons. Part of winning big has been winning small, and for Miami that's included dominating the middle portions of games. The Hurricanes have the No. 1 point differential in the second quarter in all of FBS (+95) and No. 3 point differential in the third quarter (+57). Miami is also No. 3 nationally this season in "middle 8" scoring (the last four minutes of the second quarter and the first four minutes of the third quarter), with a +7.6-point average on the season. TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Miami vs. North Carolina prediction, picks Miami's first season of ACC play featured a trip to Chapel Hill on Halloween night to take on a North Carolina team that was 3-4 overall, with four 20-plus-point losses to ranked teams. The Hurricanes, ranked No. 4 at the time, were 6-0 and looking to establish themselves as the class of the ACC, having joined the conference just a few years removed from a national championship. A lot has been made about Miami's struggles in the last five meetings, but the Hurricanes' issues with the Heels date back to the very beginning of their time in the league, and Connor Barth's game-winning kick to seal the spooky upset. Bill Belichick and North Carolina's defense can get enough stops to keep this close, and with Notre Dame on deck, the Hurricanes might not be in the mindset to push this game deep into the evening. picks.blurb: UNC vs Miami prediction: Will Bill Belichick's Tar Heels upset No. 1 Hurricanes? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Rodd Baxley, Fayetteville Observer Fri, October 30, 2026 at 9:04 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time in 22 years, UNC football is hosting a top-five Miami team on Halloween weekend at Kenan Stadium. Bill Belichick's Tar Heels (4-3, 2-2 ACC) host the top-ranked Hurricanes (7-0, 5-0) on Saturday, Oct. 31 (7:30 p.m., ABC), with hopes of earning the program's first victory against the No. 1 team in the nation. UNC earned a 31-28 against No. 4 Miami on Halloween weekend in 2004, getting a game-winning field goal from Wilmington native Connor Barth. The Tar Heels are aiming for their sixth straight win against the Hurricanes, who haven't beaten UNC since 2018. But the Heels are 0-11 in games against the top-ranked team in the country. Watch UNC-Miami on Fubo RED-ZONE PROBLEM: UNC football red-zone rate doesn't tell full story for Bill Belichick's Tar Heels "Miami, they're the No. 1 team in the country and they should be," UNC coach Bill Belichick said during his weekly press conference. "Really impressive. (Miami coach Mario Cristobal has) done, as usual, a great job down there. They're a very well-balanced team, pretty much do everything well." Here are some things to know, players to watch and a score prediction for UNC vs. Miami. Miami QB Darian Mensah, Miami WR Malachi Toney are Heisman Trophy hopefuls Conversations about the Hurricanes start with quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney, two players hoping to be in New York City for the Heisman Trophy ceremony. Mensah leads the nation in completion percentage (81.4%) with 22 touchdowns and one interception. Toney paces all pass-catchers with 66 catches for 952 yards and 11 TDs. If UNC fans want a sign of hope, Mensah was limited to 175 passing yards and a touchdown last season for Duke vs. the Tar Heels. Still, this Miami offense is operating in a different stratosphere with an average of nearly 50 points per game. Mark Fletcher, Miami rushing offense can't be overlooked by UNC In addition to a potent passing attack, Miami has the 18th rushing offense nationally at 211 yards per game. The Hurricanes have gained at least 119 rushing yards in each of their seven games, including more than 257 yards against Florida State. Running backs Mark Fletcher and Javian Mallory have combined for 858 yards and 14 rushing TDs, averaging nearly 7 yards per carry. The Tar Heels are 91st in rushing defense, allowing an average of nearly 155 yards per game on the ground. The last time it played a top-five opponent, UNC allowed No. 5 Notre Dame to rack up 241 rushing yards. UNC defense, special teams need special play to beat Hurricanes If the Tar Heels are going to pull off an upset against the Hurricanes, it'll likely involve a special play from the defense or special teams. UNC made it a one-point game against Notre Dame with a game-changing kickoff return for a touchdown and nearly had a ice-the-game fumble recovery for a TD in a win at Pitt. With eight takeaways (5 interceptions, 3 fumble recoveries), UNC is 75th nationally. The Heels have to create some chaos for the Hurricanes to keep the crowd in it and put some game pressure on the visitors. UNC vs Miami score prediction Miami 38, UNC 18 : The Tar Heels have improved enough to close in on bowl eligibility, but the Hurricanes are in a different neighborhood as national championship contenders. In what will serve as a gauge-where-we-are game for Bill Belichick's program, "The U" will pull away in the second half.
