The No. 1 Miami Hurricanes will travel to Chapel Hill, North Carolina to take on the Tar Heels for a spooky Halloween night match-up. UM (7-0, 5-0) has lost five straight to UNC and the Hurricanes have emphasized the importance of not looking ahead to next week's prime time game against top five Notre Dame. North Carolina (4-3, 2-2) is coming off a 31-30 overtime loss to Syracuse. The Tar Heels have already matched their 2025 win total in year two of the Bill Belichick era. Kickoff for Saturday's game is set for 7:30 p.m. EST. The game will be televised on ABC. Miami enters the game viewed as the most well rounded team in the country, averaging 49 points per game (1st in FBS) while the defense is allowing 15.3 points per game (11th in FBS). The Hurricanes average 551 yards per game (1st) while converting 54.5 percent on third down (5th) with an 81 percent red-zone touchdown rate (7th). UM's defense allows 299 yards per game (21st) while opponents convert 34 percent of their opportunities (35th) with a red-zone touchdown rate allowed of 35.7 percent (4th). UM gets flagged for 62.86 penalty yards per game, which ranks 83rd in the country. North Carolina is averaging 24.4 points per game (95th) while the defense is the strength of the team, allowing 20.9 points per game (41st) The Tar Heels averaging 335 yards per game and convert 40.5 percent of their third downs. The red-zone touchdown rate for UNC is 62.5 percent, which ranks 69th nationally. UNC's defense allows 327 yards per game (85th) and allows opponents to convert 43.1 percent of the time (115th). The red-zone touchdown rate allowed checks in at 47.8 percent, which ranks 22nd nationally. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, Miami is a 14.5 point favorite. UM's last victory over the Tar Heels came in 2018. North Carolina won the last match-up between the two schools in 2023, 41-31, in Chapel Hill. Read on for a closer look at how Miami and North Carolina match up on paper going into Saturday night's game. (Photo: Getty) Miami's passing operation is the most efficient in the country with the Hurricanes completing 80.9 percent of attempts (1st in FBS), 10.4 yards/attempt (2nd), 0.56 EPA per drop-back (1st), 202.1 passing efficiency (1st), and a first down or touchdown on 48.7% of attempts (1st). Quarterback Darian Mensah has thrown for 2,151 yards with 22 touchdowns and one interception. He is coming off a performance against Pittsburgh in which he completed 31-of-37 passes for 387 yards and four touchdowns. Miami's passing attack is not a downfield-heavy attack. The average depth of target is only 7.8 air yards (99th), but receivers are creating 6.5 YAC per catch (22nd) — 1,211 of their 2,385 yards have come after the catch. Quick, accurate throws to playmakers in space. Slot receiver Malachi Toney is the top target for the Hurricanes, catching 66 passes for 952 yards and 11 touchdowns. Toney is the most efficient receiver in the country, catching 89 percent of his targets while not dropping a pass this year. Cooper Barkate is second on the team with 301 yards and four touchdowns. UM's pass protection is solid with a 25.7 percent pressure rate allowed (26th) and a 3.8 percent sack rate (25th). Mensah does a good job of getting the ball out quick at a 2.59 time to throw, which is 21st fastest in the country. Center Ryan Rodriguez grades out as the best pass blocker for the Hurricanes with two pressures allowed while right tackle Matthew McCoy has allowed nine pressures and one sack on the year. Left tackle Samson Okunlola has allowed 14 pressures and one sack while true freshman Ben Congdon has allowed ten pressures and two sacks on the year. The North Carolina pass defense is statistically mediocre. The Tar Heels allow 218 pass yards per game, 6.3 yards per attempt (33rd), a 84.1 passer rating allowed (56th), a 57.7 percent defensive success rate (91st), and a bottom-tier 43.1 percent third-down conversion rate allowed (116th). UNC's pass rush doesn't generate much pressure with a 29.3 percent pressure rate (93rd), a 5.5 percent sack rate (91st), and 2.6 seconds to pressure (93rd). The Tar Heels blitz on only 21.2 percent of drop-backs (102nd) — a conservative, rush-four approach that hasn't generated much. Defensive lineman Xavier Lewis leads the Tar Heels with 28 pressures and seven sacks. At 6-feet-4 and 200 pounds, safety Greg Smith is a rangy safety, who has been targeted 16 times, allowing only seven receptions for 56 yards with one touchdown while picking off there passes. North Carolina primarily runs Cover-3 (31 percent of the time) and they limit the depth of target at 6.5 air yards per attempt. Edge: Miami. UNC's pass defense wants to keep everything in front of them, but that plays right into Miami's hands with a passing game that thrives on YAC. Miami has already seen a lot of Cover 3 (33% of snaps) and zone (68%) this season and torched it, so UNC's base scheme offers nothing unfamiliar. The Miami Hurricanes run game brings balance to an explosive passing attack. UM averaged 211 rushing yards per game, which ranks 18th best in the country, as it complements a passing offense that is the most efficient in FBS. The Hurricanes average 5.6 yards per carry (10th in FBS) while totaling 20 rushing touchdowns (11th). The strength of the Miami rushing attack is contact balance. UM averages 3.94 yards per carry after contact (9th) while being credited with avoiding 82 tackles (7th). Senior Mark Fletcher is RB1 while totaling 414 yards and seven touchdowns and averaging 5.1 yards per carry. Fletcher is the hammer in UM's backfield, averaging 4.01 yards per carry after contact and a 38 percent tackle avoidance rate, which ranks 11th best n the country. True freshman Javian Mallory is a star in the making, leading the team with 444 rushing yards and seven touchdowns while averaging 7.5 yards per carry. Mallory averages 4.75 yards per carry after contact. Run blocking is the strength of this 2026 Miami Hurricanes offensive line. UM's offensive line does a solid job of creating yards for the running backs before contact at 2.13 yards before contact per rush, which ranks 34th nationally. The Hurricanes allow a tackle for loss on only 3.8 percent of their snaps, which is tied for the best in FBS. The one soft spot of UM's rushing attack is 3rd-down rush conversions are only 50 percent (61st). Short-yardage hasn't been automatic. The UNC run defense is below average with marks of 154.7 rush yards per game allowed (91st), 3.9 yards per carry (62nd), +5.5 rush EPA allowed (85th), 56.8 percent defensive rush success rate (96th), and a first down allowed on 24.5 percent of carries (86th). The primary issue for the North Carolina run defense is tackling. UNC allows just 1.25 yards before contact (37th — the front is actually getting to the ballcarrier) but 3.52 yards after contact (110th). They've missed 51 tackles on run plays. They get there and don't finish. Opponents convert 58.3 percent of third-down rushes (124th). They also almost never go to a heavy short-yardage package (8.3% of snaps, 2nd fewest), sitting in nickel 58 percent of the time — a light box against a team that wants to run downhill. North Carolina's defensive front has totaled only 29 tackles for loss on the season with DL Xavier Lewis the only real disruptor at 12 tackles for loss on the season. Linebacker Derek McDonald has totaled 72 tackles and two tackles for loss. Defensive tackle Leroy Jackson does a good job of logging the middle of the line of scrimmage. Edge: Miami. UM's identity (win after contact) attacks UNC's identity flaw (lose after contact) head-on. A team that's 9th in YAC/rush against a defense that's 110th in YAC allowed is the whole story.Opposing teams know that UNC's run defense is poor, attempting 39 runs per game against the Tar Heels, which is one of the highest rates in the country. TE Jelani Thurman (Photo: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images) The North Carolina passing attack is below average. Quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. is 124-of-207 (59.9%, 98th) on the season for 1,553 yards with 11 touchdowns and five interceptions. He is averaging 7.5 yards per attempt (67th), with a passer efficiency rating of 135.6 (78th), 0.12 EPA per dropback (67th). The UNC passing attack is not explosive with only 19 completions of 20+ (99th) and one of 50+ yards. The average depth of target is 7.9 yards (94th) — it's a short-to-intermediate attack. There are two clear top targets for North Carolina in the passing game. Wide receiver Jordan Shipp, who lines up both on the outside and in the slot, is the clear number one target with 41 receptions for 543 yards. But the Hurricanes allow 239 pass yards per game (107th) because nobody can run on Miami, so opponents throw 35.6 times a game (126th most). The pass rush is the identity of this phase of defense. The Hurricanes generate pressure in 2.3 seconds, which is the fastest in the FBS, and a pressure rate of 36.8 percent (23rd), while totaling 20 sacks (18th). Miami will blitz 34.6 percent of the time (20th). DE Marquise Lightfoot (23 pressures, 5 sacks) and DE Damon Wilson II (24 pressures, 11 QB hits, 3.5 sacks) are the edge duo that apply the most pass rushing punch while DL Armondo Blount adds 17 pressures. From a coverage standpoint, the Hurricanes run Cover-3 on 38 percent of their snaps and Cover-1 21 percent of the time. He does have an interception he returned for a touchdown. Edge: Miami. away.headline: Notre Dame can survive its latest injury wave against Navy, but Miami is different
away.blurb: Notre Dame football’s “ next man up ” philosophy should be enough to get Marcus Freeman through Navy despite another crowded injury report. But with DJ McKinney out, Brauntae Johnson still sidelined, and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa among the questionable players, Chris Ash needs that list to shrink considerably before Miami arrives. Despite the Fighting Irish coming off a bye week , head coach Marcus Freeman detailed several injuries that will hit Chris Ash’s unit hard. The good news is that none of the players who will miss time or be questionable are ones the team should need against Navy. The question is how healthy some of these guys will be in two weeks against Miami. On Monday afternoon, Freeman said McKinney is out for the Navy game with an ankle injury. That’s never good news, as that kind of injury can stick around for a while. A cornerback who can’t make cuts won’t keep up with receivers. That’s not an issue against Navy, but against Miami, especially Malachi Toney, it’s a big one. Another big injury update: safety Brauntae Johnson is still out. Notre Dame has hoped he’d be out for “just a couple of weeks” after he was injured in the first half of the season opener. However, with the season now in Week 8, people have to start worrying about whether he will play this year. The injury list doesn’t end there. Freeman said that tight end Cooper Flanagan (hamstring), linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa (thumb), defensive lineman Loghan Thomas (shoulder), and cornerback Mark Zackery IV (concussion) are all questionable. Of course, of all the injuries that might just be cautionary, KVA’s questionable status is the most likely situation where he could have been fine to play if Miami was this week. Notre Dame should absolutely be able to beat Navy even without Viliamu-Asa in the lineup. The injury that should make Notre Dame faithful most worried is DJ McKinney’s. The transfer cornerback was hurt late in the game against BYU , and the bye week apparently wasn't enough time for him to heal and get back to 100%. Notre Dame football defensive injuries create bigger questions for Miami than Navy Because Notre Dame knows Navy won’t tax its cornerbacks much, sitting McKinney this week isn’t a shock. It’s even possible that if this were Miami week , they’d be working to get him back on the field. The Irish won’t push it against the Midshipmen. The most interesting note in that group is that Notre Dame took quite a bit of heat for not playing Viliamu-Asa more against BYU. North Carolina fans are ready for the college basketball season, but a couple of things need to be considered before Monday night as it takes on Western Carolina. North Carolina should be able to win this game no matter who's on the court for them, but it's also important to note that some injuries are currently being factored in. The biggest is Matt Able, the North Carolina State transfer expected to be one of the better players on the roster this season. Able missed the exhibition game against Charlotte, though it hasn't been reported yet what happened. According to Rodd Baxley, who was at the game, the injury didn't look noticeable. Baxley added that he was on the sidelines during UNC's warmups, and it didn't seem to be too big of a problem. “Able, an N.C. State transfer, is one of 11 newcomers on coach Michael Malone's first roster in Chapel Hill. The 6-foot-5, 200-pound guard is a starter in the backcourt alongside Virginia Tech transfer Neo Avdalas and Utah transfer Terrence Brown… “Able's injury doesn't look noticeable. He was on the sidelines during UNC's warmups ahead of the game. Still, it's another missed opportunity for Able to get game action with a revamped roster and a backcourt that includes Utah transfer Terrence Brown, along with Virginia Tech transfer Neo Avdalas. Isaiah Denis missed the Indiana exhibition game with a minor injury,” Baxley wrote . Able, who withdrew from the NBA draft last year to go to North Carolina, is expected to be one of the ACC's better players this season. He's coming off a decent freshman year at NC State, averaging 8.8 points, 3.4 rebounds, and shooting 35.5% from three-point range on 4.1 attempts per game. He has areas to improve, including as a passer, but there's a lot to like about the young man, and the hope is that he'll be what everybody knows he can be. Hopefully, this is just a small thing, and North Carolina can get it under control before it plays on Monday night. If not, it's fine if he misses a few games.

picks.blurb: Ohio State On SI Week 9 Picks: Can Buckeyes Overcome Spooky Road Test vs. USC? Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB Happy Halloween, Ohio State fans . The Buckeyes (6-1, 4-0 Big Ten) will try to maintain their No. 2 ranking Saturday night and attempt to knock off a desperate USC Trojans (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten) team still fighting for their CFP lives. With kickoff drawing closer, how does a Buckeyes team no longer led by quarterback Julian Sayin fare on the road? Scroll to find this week’s staff predictions, as I am all alone in first place at 7-0 so far this season. Ohio State @ USC Week 9 Game Details Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Parris Campbell (21) runs the ball as USC Trojans cornerback Isaiah Langley (24) tackles during the third quarter of the Goodyear Cotton Bowl Classic between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the USC Trojans on Friday, December 29, 2017 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. Odds : Ohio State -6.5 ; over/under is 51.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum – Los Angeles, Calif. Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 88-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. USC: 2017 Cotton Bowl: Ohio State won 24-7, when the Trojans were still members of the Pac-12. USC leads the all-time series 13-10-1 since 1937. Ohio State so far this season: 6-1 (4-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando : 7-0 Dylan Buganski : 6-1 Rafael Zamorano : 4-1 (no pick in Week 6 or Week 7) Chip Minnich : 5-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 21, USC 17 After a week off, Ohio State continues its quest for a Big Ten and national title. It’ll just be without Julian Sayin as its starting quarterback. Since Sayin went down, Ohio State on SI (and I included) have done our best to bring Buckeye Nation as many perspectives as possible as the season resumes Saturday night in Los Angeles against the USC Trojans. Given the parity in this year's wacky college football season, the Buckeyes have yet to have a true reality-check moment. This week isn’t it either. The Badgers, who play the Iowa Hawkeyes earlier in the day’s action, suffocated the Trojans in all areas last week in Madison in one of the sport’s most shocking upsets. Although Halloween night could call for a spooky outcome (pun purposely intended), it’s hard to pick against Ohio State in Big Ten play, regardless of who the quarterback ends up being, until it loses in league play. So far, I’m the lone undefeated picker this season, so riding the hot hand with coach Ryan Day’s team against a depleted Trojans bunch seems like a smart pick (although all-time series history says otherwise). Rafael Zamorano: Ohio State 24, USC 14 Ohio State has reached the crux of its season, not necessarily because of where they stand in Big Ten competition at this point in its schedule, but because we don’t know for sure what the Buckeyes will look like without star quarterback Julian Sayin for the foreseeable future. Not to take anything away from the 6-2 Trojans, but what was originally supposed to be a road game against a solid-but-not-elite conference opponent has now shifted its focus entirely on how the Buckeyes will look with a freshman starting at quarterback, be it true freshman Luke Fahey or redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair. Having said that, Ohio State still wields a deeper and more talented roster overall, headlined by the best player in the game, wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. The Buckeyes’ staff has more than enough resources to work with to keep whichever quarterback ends up starting well protected scheme-wise. Look for a lot of quick passes and screens on offense, while the defense figures out a way to pressure Jayden Maiava into committing mistakes, just like Wisconsin did last week. With the Buckeyes being favored by a touchdown on the spread (-7), I’m picking them to cover thanks to another solid performance on defense. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 24, USC 21 The Wisconsin Badgers’ 24-7 win over USC last Saturday has Ohio State fans understandably wondering whether the Buckeyes will follow a comparable game plan. I am guessing that Luke Fahey will be the starting quarterback, and that the coaching staff has emphasized to Fahey to play efficiently in a style reminiscent of when Julian Sayin made his first start at home vs. Texas in 2025. The USC defensive line has the pass rushing ability to get after an opposing quarterback, and I believe Fahey will use his legs to get out of the pocket and make positive yards to keep drives alive. Ohio State's defense is going to be tested all game against a formidable USC offense, despite the issues that the Trojans had last week in Madison. Maybe it's wishful thinking on my part, but this game has some serious Tresselball vibes for me going into Saturday night against an USC team that has its back to the wall. Yards and points may be difficult for the Buckeyes to earn, but I believe the Buckeyes will exhale when Connor Hawkins makes a late field goal in the final minutes of the contest. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, USC 14 For the first time during Ryan Day’s tenure as Ohio State head coach, a backup quarterback will start for the Buckeyes in a Big Ten matchup. It is still unknown if that starter will be true freshman Luke Fahey, or former 5-star sophomore Tavien St. Clair. Although, what is known coming into this matchup is that the USC defense has been one of the worst defenses against the pass in the Big Ten this season. picks.blurb: Ohio State vs. USC prediction: Why Buckeyes are in danger at Trojans - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Ohio State vs. USC prediction: Why Buckeyes are in danger at Trojans Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Ohio State has been tabbed as a national championship favorite since this summer, but a major change at quarterback could make things interesting against USC this week. One of the more intriguing matchups on the Week 9 college football calendar finds the Buckeyes going on the road against the Trojans without Julian Sayin under center. How does that affect what happens in this battle of college football blue bloods? How Ohio State can win Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates a touchdown with with wide receiver Devin McCuin (3) during the NCAA football game against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. on Oct. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Regardless of concerns at quarterback, Ohio State has the more complete statistical profile, particularly on defense. The Buckeyes are allowing just 13.4 points and 264.3 total yards per game, ranking fourth and sixth nationally, respectively. Their run defense has been especially effective, giving up only 92.9 rushing yards per game. It should have a decisive edge against a USC ground game that is 105th in FBS and totaling just 131 yards on average. Offensively, Jeremiah Smith has been spectacular yet again. The undefendable wide receiver and Heisman favorite has 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns on 52 catches. Even without Sayin, Ohio State can lean on its defense, establish Bo Jackson in the trenches, slow the game down, get the football into Smith's hands, and let him create after the catch. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Maybe relying on USC's defense to win a game hasn't always been a great idea. But they're in a very good position to exploit the Buckeyes' uncertainty at quarterback. Applying enough pressure on the edges to rattle Sayin's replacement could give this talented offense enough breathing room to make this interesting. The Trojans are averaging 303.6 passing yards per game, ranking 10th nationally, with quarterback Jayden Maiava throwing for 2,303 yards and 19 touchdowns. USC also converts 50.5 percent of its third downs, the 14th-best rate in the country. That ability to sustain drives could be important against an Ohio State defense that has allowed opponents to convert just 38 percent of third downs. The Trojans need Maiava to protect the football and attack downfield over top OSU's front line defenders. Defensively, USC must pressure the inexperienced Buckeyes quarterback and prevent him from developing any early rhythm. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 9's biggest games Who wins, and why? Make no mistake: the absence of Julian Sayin distributing to the Buckeyes' talented wideouts is a real problem. USC, whatever its defensive lapses in the Riley era, has a legitimate opportunity to make this uncomfortable. Still, Ohio State has a significant defensive advantage overall, allowing just 13 points per game and has an important edge countering the Trojans' ground game that can reduce that offense to one dimension. USC will have opportunities, but Ohio State's defensive consistency ultimately proves to be the edge in the second half. The Big Lead prediction: Ohio State 30, USC 23

This game is a major test as it will be Ohio State's first game since Julian Sayin suffered his significant right arm injury in the Buckeyes' October 17 victory over Indiana. Head coach Ryan Day has not announced whether Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair will be under center for the Buckeyes (6-1), but it is clear that Ohio State faces a test against the 6-2 Trojans. The Buckeyes are 6.5-point favorites against the Trojans and they appear to have multiple advantages as USC has significant defensive issues. Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL Bears In The Pros Baylor stares down UCF on Friday night as they try to avoid a third straight loss. The Bears torched UCF in Waco last November 30-3 and will try to rinse and repeat on the road. UCF is undefeated on their home turf and is coming off a dramatic victory over No. 2 BYU, making them 1.5-point favorites over the Bears. Here are three predictions for Joe Klanderman's debut in Baylor's Week 9 matchup: It will still feel like Aranda's team The Bears have parted ways with Dave Aranda after seven years, and Joe Klanderman has stepped into the interim head coach role. Klanderman had just five days to get this team into shape before UCF. While his methods and leadership may be strong, it is surely hard to turn a football team on its head in less than a week. With offensive coordinator Jake Spavital still in charge of the offensive playcalling, I doubt Baylor is going to look dramatically different than they did against Kansas. UCF enters Week 9 fresh off the biggest win in program history, while Baylor navigates the fallout from firing its head coach. It's an electrifying Big 12 matchup on Friday, Oct. 30, and my Baylor vs. UCF prediction backs the Bears to rain on the Knights' parade. Check out my latest college football picks ahead of tonight's 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff on ESPN. TOP PICK Who will win Baylor vs UCF: Baylor +1.5 UCF is coming off a win over No. 2 BYU, marking the program's first victory over an AP top-five team. Now, the Knights have a massive target on their backs as they draw a Baylor team that just fired head coach Dave Aranda after nearly seven seasons. There's nothing more glorious than the coach-firing bump . This Knights team isn't all that impressive, either. Outside of Week 8, UCF hasn't been competitive against quality competition, with losses to Pitt, Houston, and Oklahoma State. Its other three wins came against TCU, Georgia State, and Bethune-Cookman. With that win over BYU clearly serving as its Super Bowl, the Knights should regress this week against the Bears. Baylor or nothing. Take the Bears on the moneyline if you don't want to lay any juice. Baylor vs UCF Over/Under pick: Over 47.5 Despite expecting the Knights to come out a tad sluggish, this game should feature plenty of scoring opportunities — especially with how fast Baylor likes to play. The Bears will likely generate the most points in this matchup, which is why I like them overall. UCF ranks 118th nationally in passing yards allowed per game , giving Baylor quarterback DJ Lagway a chance to carve up this mediocre pass defense. The Bears average nearly 270 passing yards per game this season, ranking 20th nationally. Baylor also boasts a strong defense, allowing just 18.3 points and about 380 total yards per game. Even with the Bears' stout defense, the Knights should still find a way to get on the board. In the end, though, Baylor should do most of the heavy lifting to push this total over the finish line. Baylor vs UCF combo The Bears should enter this game with a little extra pep in their step after their coach was fired, looking to take down a team coming off its Super Bowl a week ago. Baylor plays extremely fast and should be able to jump out to an early lead and keep its foot on the gas. I'll combo Baylor +1.5, first-half +2.5, and Over 47.5 for a fun 4.78x sweat! Baylor first half +2.5 Baylor vs UCF prop: Baylor 1H +2.5 If you're looking to get in and out of this matchup, Baylor +2.5 in the first half may be the look for you. The Knights could come out of the gate sluggish after beating the Cougars, while Baylor's fast-paced offense should overwhelm this Knights defense. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 9 Space Game Preview: Baylor Bears @ UCF Knights - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em 2026 Week 9 Space Game Preview: Baylor Bears @ UCF Knights ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights reacts after a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steve Helwick Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:12 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, October 30 at 7:30 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: Baylor (-1.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Baylor leads, 2-1 Last meeting: Baylor 30, UCF 3 — November 1, 2025 Current streak: Baylor, 2 (2023-25) Setting the scene Baylor and UCF have only met three times, but there is no shortage of iconic moments between these programs. UCF entered the 2013 Fiesta Bowl as a 13.5-point underdog to Big 12 champion Baylor. However, Blake Bortles led the Knights to an electrifying 52-42 victory on New Year's Day, sealing the program's first-ever AP Top 10 finish. Ten years later, UCF held a 35-7 lead in the late third quarter over Baylor, but the Bears rallied with 29 unanswered, surviving a wild fourth down conversion and a 59-yard field goal attempt to hold onto a 36-35 win. Perhaps another memorable finish awaits as the programs meet in Orlando for the 10th annual Space Game. UCF continues one of college football's most recognizable modern traditions, rebranding to the "Citronauts" for a night and donning space-themed alternate uniforms as a nod to the university's aeronautical roots. The Citronauts are one of the better teams in college football history, owning an 8-1 record in Space Games and outscoring opponents by an aggregate result of 432-189: 2017 – UCF 63, East Carolina 21 2018 – UCF 52, Temple 40 2019 – UCF 44, Houston 29 2020 – UCF 51, Tulane 34 2021 – UCF 24, Memphis 7 2022 – UCF 70, Temple 13 2023 – UCF 45, Oklahoma State 3 2024 – UCF 56, Arizona 12 2025 – Houston 30, UCF 27 However, Houston defeated UCF in last year's Space Game, spoiling the Citronauts' perfect record. UCF, coming off its first top-5 victory in program history, aims to recapture its galactic momentum as Baylor strolls into the Bounce House. Baylor Bears outlook WACO, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 19: Defensive Coordinator Joe Klanderman of the Baylor Bears yells from the sideline during the second quarter during the game against the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs on September 19, 2026 at the McLane Stadium in Waco, Texas. (Photo by Hanna Kotlarek/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) fired head coach Dave Aranda in the middle of his seventh season in Waco. Aranda's tenure was quite volatile, featuring highs of a 12-2 finish and Big 12 championship in 2021, but lows including a 3-9 record in 2023. The Bears lacked consistency under Aranda, improving or declining by at least three wins in every year from 2019 through 2025. Baylor moves forward with interim Joe Klanderman, who also retains his defensive coordinator duties. In year one on campus, Klanderman has done a stellar job reforming Baylor's defense. He implemented a 3-3-5 base scheme and vastly improved the unit, allowing them to skyrocket from 122nd to 19th in scoring defense and 122nd to 22nd in run defense. The Bears let up just 16.1 points per game, and last Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas was the first time they surrendered more than 17 points all season. The defense showed promise even in losing efforts, falling 17-16 to Auburn and 17-6 to TCU. Baylor is the best in the Big 12 at getting to the quarterback and its 3.9 sacks per game rank third nationally. There isn't one dominant pass rusher, rather, it's a concerted effort. Edge rusher Garrick Ponder leads the charge with 4.0 sacks while safeties Daniel Cobbs and Bo Onu are tied for second with 3.0 apiece. With great pressure comes great chaos, and Baylor is producing takeaways at a high rate. The team ranks 15th nationally with 13 takeaways, and strong safety Micah Gifford has been omnipresent with three interceptions and two fumble recoveries. While the passing defense has more interceptions than touchdowns allowed, and forces opponents to a 59.8 completion rate, Baylor still allows 236 passing yards per game, which ranks 103rd nationally. Teams regularly hit explosives on the Bears, which have given up 13 passes of 30 yards or greater through seven games. Last season, Baylor excelled offensively and struggled on defense. This year, the opposite is true. Outside of the 55-19 rout at Arizona State, the Bears have not been able to consistently generate points. They scored 24 or fewer points in four of seven games, and all three losses were attribute to a lack of scoring. Still, quarterback DJ Lagway has moved the ball well for the nation's 24th-ranked passing offense. The veteran starter averages 270 passing yards per game, delivering nine touchdowns and four interceptions. Efficiency has been an issue through the air though, and Baylor checks in at 124th in the FBS with a 56.4 completion rate. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman operates as the main target. His 58 receptions are the second-most in the country and his 678 receiving yards rank second in the Big 12. Louis Brown and Jayden McGowan are among Lagway's other frequented options. Baylor hasn't been as lethal on the ground, still awaiting its first 90-yard rusher of the season. The Bears were held to 54 rushing yards against TCU and 122 against Kansas — a significant reason Baylor enters Orlando on a two-game losing streak. UCF Knights outlook ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights celebrates a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) is coming off a win for the ages. Although the Knights won multiple New Year's Six bowls and secured an NCAA-recognized national championship in 2017, last Saturday's double overtime triumph over No. 2 BYU was the program's first-ever top-5 victory in history. It was the long-awaited signature win of Scott Frost's second tenure in Orlando and restored energy into a fanbase, which will certainly show up in droves for the annual Space Game. There were moments throughout the BYU game where it appeared UCF missed a golden opportunity for an upset. However, the Knights stayed the course and won just their second October game in their last 13 tries. One of the heroes last week was quarterback Keyone Jenkins, who threw for 293 yards and three touchdowns, while rushing for an additional score in the 39-31 win. After witnessing several strong performances by the FIU transfer, Frost named Jenkins the starting quarterback moving forward, even though original starter Alonza Barnett III has recovered from a Week 2 hamstring injury. UCF has received stronger support from the passing attack in recent weeks, which has been efficient. The Knights have thrown 13 touchdowns against four interceptions, while completing 66.5 percent of attempts this year. It hasn't been the most explosive unit, completing just seven passes spanning 30 yards and two spanning 40, but Jenkins has allowed the Knights to piece together methodical possessions. The run game has been the hallmark of UCF's offense all season. Running back Duke Watson is eighth in the Big 12 in rushing and averages 6.8 yards per carry. Landen Chambers has also stepped up from the backfield lately, scoring two touchdowns in last week's win over BYU. But the true emerging star in UCF's offense is true freshman wide receiver Tyren Hornes. After being underutilized in September, Hornes has become one of the top options for the Knights, producing 137 yards on six receptions last Saturday. He now ranks second on the team in receiving yards behind Josh Derry, who leads all Knight receivers in catches (34), yards (358), and touchdowns (3). Although the last two weeks were more offensive oriented games, UCF has been best on the defensive side this year. The Knights allow 23.0 points per game, allow just 3.2 yards per rushing attempt, and hold opponents to a completion rate of 58.9 percent. However, UCF must play the Space Game without arguably its best defensive player. Strong safety Demari Henderson suffered an injury in overtime against BYU, and the team will miss his production, which includes 35 tackles, two interceptions, and five pass breakups. The Knights still have several veteran faces in the secondary including cornerbacks Antione Jackson and Jayden Bellamy, who both have one interception and one forced fumble on the season. Thanks to these defensive backs, UCF is a plus-5 in the turnover battle this season. Can UCF avoid a letdown after an emotional win? Signature wins haven't been easy to follow up in college football this season. Auburn beat Georgia and then lost by 21 to LSU at home. BYU took down Notre Dame and then dropped an overtime thriller to UCF a week later. Ole Miss' triumph over LSU was followed by a thrashing at the hands of Florida. And so on. Baylor also had an eventful week, as the Bears move on from head coach Dave Aranda and now must respond with an interim head coach in a hostile Orlando environment. The Bears' defense has been consistently sound this year, and UCF may struggle to come close to its Space Game average of 48 points per game. The defenses control this matchup, and the Bears prevent a successful launch with a game-winning field goal in the final minute. Prediction: Baylor 24, UCF 21

picks.headline: Predicting Final Score of Baylor Bears vs. UCF Knights in Week 9 Without Dave Aranda
picks.blurb: Predicting Final Score of Baylor Bears vs. UCF Knights in Week 9 Without Dave Aranda - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop, Blake Hollingsworth, Brad Teague & Tyler Gillum Fri, October 30, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's been a disastrous two weeks for the Baylor Bears. After dominating Arizona State and looking like the Bears could be a real threat, Baylor suffered back-to-back losses to TCU and Kansas, dropping the Bears to 4-3 on the season . The loss to Kansas also ended the Dave Aranda era in Waco. In his seventh season, Aranda was fired and Joe Klanderman will lead the Bears for the remainder of the season as the interim head coach . Klanderman looks to reignite the Baylor Bears and have a strong finish to the season. Baylor will look to get back into the win column on Friday night when the Bears take on UCF . Here's how the staff of Baylor on SI sees the game going. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Baylor's defense has been great this season and Klanderman has re-established the Bears' defense. But you have to wonder if there will be any setbacks from Dave Aranda not being on the sidelines any longer and Klanderman taking on the head coach role, while calling the defense. UCF has a good offense and Keyone Jenkins has been legit . The Knights just beat BYU and a hangover is certainly possible, but it's not like Baylor has been playing great football. What worries me is the Bears' offensive line. DJ Lagway has been asked to do everything for this offense, and the offensive line can't block for the run game. If Baylor can't run the ball again, it's going to be tough sledding. I look for the home team to make one too many plays. Final score: UCF 27, Baylor 24 Baylor comes off a tough loss to Kansas and has a shorter week facing off against a UCF team that just beat the number 2 ranked team in the country. Should be mostly a passing game given the defenses in this matchup. Baylor has struggled to get the run game going and UCF has had one of the best run defenses in the country right now. Expect a high air-raid offense from both sides, and multiple touchdowns. Baylor will be in their first game without head coach Aranda after getting let go Sunday. My guess is that they will pull one together and slightly outscore this team coming off a big win. Final score: Baylor 30, UCF 23 After the past two weeks saw Baylor lose to TCU and Kansas, fire Dave Aranda, name Joe Klanderman interim head coach, and have a shortened week of preparation for their Friday night contest against UCF, the Bears are up against the wall in terms of their season. They've officially hit the big red "panic" button on the season and fired Aranda in hopes of seemingly not losing the entire fan base. However, the competition still remains, and even with Aranda no longer with the team, the offense is still the same squad that has been struggling to produce since returning to play after the bye week. Baylor's defense is going to cause havoc for UCF's QB Keyone Jenkins and probably even record another 4+ SK 7+ TFL game. Potentially even forcing Jenkins into throwing an interception or two, the outcome of this game won't be the fault of the Bears' defense. There's only so much one side of the ball can do, after all. If the Bears O-line remains unable to successfully push back the opposing D-line, it's going to again lead to three-and-outs or otherwise quickly ended drives. Not to mention that an unsuccessful O-line will inevitably force DJ Lagway into uncomfortable throws and rushed decisions against UCF's team currently in the top 20 in the nation with a +5 turnover margin. Penalties have been a big problem for the Bears this season, especially last week, totaling a dozen for 116 yards. Averaging 74 yards a game in penalties is rough and only hurts the Bears overall. However, I don't expect that trend to end any time soon, maybe not for over 100 yards, but Baylor is going to give up a lot of yards that they didn't have to again this week. I would love nothing more than to watch the offense and defense come out and click on all cylinders, but this has been a not-so-normal week. Fully expecting the Bears to be competitive, I don't however expect them to be able to overcome their recent struggles offensively. Final score: UCF 20, Baylor 17 Blake Hollingsworth Hopefully I'm wrong, but I just don't see Baylor coming out on top in interim head coach Joe Klanderman's debut. UCF is unbeaten at home and coming off a double-overtime upset of previously undefeated No. 2 BYU. DJ Lagway should have a few chances to connect on deep passes against a UCF defense allowing nearly 240 passing yards per game. However, the Knights lead the Big 12 with 12 forced turnovers, including seven interceptions, which could be a problem for a Baylor offense averaging only 17.3 points in its four Power Four matchups outside its blowout win over Arizona State. Baylor's defense will keep the game competitive per usual, but the Bears' struggles with penalties, red-zone efficiency and offensive consistency are difficult to overlook. With UCF carrying momentum into Friday's matchup, I'm picking the Knights to hand Baylor its third consecutive loss. On one side, Baylor lost on the road to Kansas in a 25-24 fight, and that was it. Head coach Dave Aranda was fired, defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman is the interim head man, and the team needs this win with a tough November coming up. However, win in Orlando, beat Iowa State at home, and boom – the Bears are bowl-eligible. UCF lost on the road to Houston and Oklahoma State, and then it changed the national landscape – and got Scott Frost his first huge win in his second round with the Knights – with a 39-31 victory over BYU. Time, Channel, Bold Prediction IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The 4-3 Baylor Bears will look to get back into the win column on Friday night when they travel to Orlando to take on the hot UCF Knights . It could be a hangover game for Scott Frost's team , as UCF took down BYU in overtime last week. That was the Cougars' first loss of the season after they upset Notre Dame the week prior. It will also mark the first game without Dave Aranda on the sideline . In his seventh season in Waco, Aranda was fired after the Bears suffered another heartbreaking loss. Rhett Armstrong's kick was blocked last Saturday and the Bears lost to Kansas, giving them two straight losses. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman has assumed the interim head coach job , but will continue to call plays for the defense. It will be interesting to see if Baylor's defense continues to play tough football, or if Klanderman adding another responsibility hits the unit. If Baylor is going to win this game, the Bears need DJ Lagway to have another big game. Unfortunately, we can't trust the Bears' run game, but that's not because of the running backs. The offensive line has been poor this season, and can't seem to open up many holes for the backs. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has garnered all the attention this season, and for good reason. He is among the top playmakers in the country, averaging nearly 100 yards per game. Freeman has been Lagway's go-to target, and UCF knows that . Freeman will get his targets and yards, but the Bears need to find another target. Louis Brown is Baylor's second-leading wide receiver, catching 22 passes for 345 yards and three touchdowns. He's had a couple of big games. In three games this season, Brown has had five or more catches, along with 62-74 yards. The Knights will try to key in on Freeman, and they won't be able to stop the short passes to Freeman, but if Lagway looks to go deep, Brown could be his man. If Baylor can get another playmaker going alongside Freeman, the Bears have a shot to really get their offense rolling. away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Being Slow to Embrace the Transfer Portal Nov 22, 2025; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Detailed view of the jersey of Baylor Bears quarterback Sawyer Robertson (13) against the Arizona Wildcats at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship.
